mainTopic: A סופר's believability, then רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's four testimonies and the גמרא on each: a גט without the wife's knowledge, a חרשת and תרומה, the stolen beam, and the stolen חטאת.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous page. A סופר who says he did not prepare the parchment לשמה is believed, unlike in רבי אמי's case, because here he knowingly loses his whole wage. Then a new משנה brings four testimonies of רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא: a חרשת married off by her father can be divorced with a גט; a קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה and her husband inherits her; a stolen beam built into a building is repaid with money because of תקנת השבים; and a stolen חטאת that is not publicly known still atones because of תיקון המזבח. In the גמרא, רבא learns from the first testimony that a גט works even if the husband calls it a loan document out of embarrassment. Next the גמרא explains why a חרשת married to a כהן may not eat any תרומה, through a chain of protective גזירות. A ברייתא shows that the beam ruling follows בית הלל against בית שמאי. Finally, עולא and רב יהודה argue about whether a stolen חטאת atones by Torah law. Their dispute depends on whether יאוש alone makes the item the robber's.

steps.title: How is this different from רבי אמי's case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the סופר is believed, because רבי אמי said a סופר is not believed in a similar case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between this case and the case of רבי אמי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just ruled that a סופר who says he did not prepare the parchment לשמה is believed. Now it asks why this differs from רבי אמי, who said a סופר is not believed in a similar claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי ruled that if a סופר says he wrote God's names not לשמה, we do not believe him, and the ספר תורה stays kosher. Here the סופר makes a similar claim about the parchment, and he is believed. Both cases involve a סופר trying to disqualify his own work, so the two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? (asks why two cases that look alike are ruled differently)
With the proper holy intention, done for the sake of the מצוה
Scribe who writes a ספר תורה

phrases.english: And what is different from the case of Rabbi Ami?
phrases.notes: רבי אמי said a סופר who claims he wrote God's names without proper intention is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by contrasting the current ruling with רבי אמי's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a סופר who says the parchment was not prepared לשמה is believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי did not believe a סופר who tried to disqualify his own work. So why should this סופר be believed?

steps.title: In this case the סופר loses his whole wage, so he is believed
steps.stepSummary: In רבי אמי's case the סופר may have lied because he thought he would lose only part of his pay. Here he loses everything, so he must be telling the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, we can say he made the same mistake as רבי ירמיה. Here, since he loses his entire wage and still comes and says it, say that he is telling the truth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing how the two cases differ. The difference is how much money the סופר knowingly gives up by making his claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אמי's case, the סופר may have mistakenly thought, as רבי ירמיה did, that he would lose only his pay for the holy names. So lying would cost him little, and he might lie just to upset the buyer. Here, a claim about the parchment wipes out his whole wage. A person does not throw away all his pay just to annoy someone, so we believe him.
steps.whatToRemember: A person is believed when his statement clearly costs him a lot. A claim that costs him little may just be an attempt to cause trouble.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: we judge whether someone is believable by asking what he gains or loses by speaking.

phrases.english: There, it is possible to say
he made the mistake of Rabbi Yirmeya.
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה thought the סופר would lose only his pay for writing God's names, not his pay for the whole scroll.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּקָא מַפְסֵיד כּוּלֵּיהּ אַגְרֵיהּ –
phrases.english: Here, since he loses his entire wage –
and he comes and says it anyway,
say that he is telling the truth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר טָעֵי בִּדְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by the size of the loss the סופר knowingly accepts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases seem the same, so the סופר should not be believed here either.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבי אמי's case the סופר may have thought he would lose only a little, so he may be lying. Here he knowingly loses everything, so he is believed.

steps.title: A deaf-mute woman married off by her father can be divorced with a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testifies that a חרשת whose father married her off can leave the marriage through a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified about a deaf-mute woman whose father married her off, that she leaves the marriage with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא reports a ruling about a חרשת whose father married her off when she was young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her father had the power to marry her off, so the marriage is valid by Torah law. A חרשת is not considered able to give legal consent. Even so, a גט still works for her, because a woman does not need to agree for a divorce to take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the beginning of a משנה)
Testified (reported a ruling he had received)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the marriage is weak because she cannot consent. Her father married her off, so it is a full Torah marriage. The ruling is that a גט still works for her.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda testified
about a deaf-mute woman whose father married her off,
that she leaves the marriage with a bill of divorce;

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins and starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרשת married off by her father can be divorced with a גט.

steps.title: A young girl married to a כהן eats תרומה, and her husband inherits her
steps.stepSummary: His second testimony: a young non-כהן girl married to a כהן may eat תרומה, and if she dies, her husband inherits her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a young girl, the daughter of a non-כהן, who married a כהן: she eats תרומה, and if she dies, her husband inherits from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second testimony. It covers a קטנה, the daughter of a non-כהן, who married a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her father has died, so she was married off by her mother or brother. That kind of marriage is valid only by rabbinic law. Even so, the רבנן treat it as a real marriage in two ways: she may eat תרומה, and her husband inherits her property.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl under the age of twelve
The daughter of a non-כהן Jew
A holy portion of produce that only a כהן's household may eat

phrases.english: And about a minor girl, the daughter of a non-priest,
who was married to a priest,
that she eats teruma,
and if she dies – her husband inherits from her;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל קְטַנָּה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second testimony in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה married to a כהן under a rabbinic marriage eats תרומה, and her husband inherits from her.

steps.title: A stolen beam built into a building is paid back with money
steps.stepSummary: His third testimony: if a stolen beam was built into a large building, the owner gets its value in money instead of the beam itself, because of תקנת השבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a stolen beam that was built into a large building: the owner takes its value, because of the rule made to help people who repent.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third testimony, about a stolen beam that is now part of a building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a thief must return the exact item he stole. Here that would mean tearing down the building to get the beam out. The רבנן made a rule, תקנת השבים, so the thief may pay its value instead. This makes it easier for a thief to repent.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic rule made to help people who repent

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of תקנת השבים opens the larger topic of rabbinic rules made for the general good, which the following material builds on.

phrases.english: And about the stolen beam
that he built into a large building,
that the owner takes its value,
because of the ordinance for the penitent;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַמָּרִישׁ הַגָּזוּל שֶׁבְּנָאוֹ בְּבִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third testimony in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner of a stolen beam built into a building receives its value in money, not the beam, because of תקנת השבים.

steps.title: Fourth testimony: a stolen sin-offering still brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testifies that a stolen חטאת, if the theft was not publicly known, still brings כפרה, because of תיקון המזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he testified about a stolen sin-offering that was not known to the public: it still atones, because of the benefit of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last of רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimonies: a stolen חטאת still works if people did not know it was stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a stolen animal should not be able to bring כפרה. Here the חכמים let it work when the theft was not publicly known, and the reason given is תיקון המזבח, the good of the altar. Steps 19–21 explain this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering, brought to gain forgiveness for certain sins
For the good of the altar, a rabbinic enactment to protect the altar's service

phrases.english: And about a stolen sin-offering
that was not known to the public
that it does atone
because of the benefit of the altar.
phrases.notes: Steps 19–21 explain what this "benefit of the altar" means.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל חַטָּאת הַגְּזוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעָה לְרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and final testimony, following the stolen beam ruling of step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen חטאת whose theft was not publicly known brings כפרה, because of תיקון המזבח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified to four rulings: a חרשת can be divorced with a גט; a קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה and is inherited by her husband; a stolen beam in a building is repaid with money because of תקנת השבים; and a stolen חטאת that is not publicly known still atones, because of תיקון המזבח.

steps.title: רבא: a divorce works even when the wife thinks she got a loan document
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the first testimony (a חרשת can be divorced) that a woman's consent is not needed. So a גט given while the husband calls it a loan document still divorces her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From the testimony of רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא we learn: if a man told witnesses, 'See this גט that I am giving her,' and then told her, 'Take this loan document,' she is divorced. Didn't רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא say we don't need her consent? Here too we don't need her consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבא draws a practical ruling from the first testimony about the חרשת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרשת cannot understand or agree, yet she can be divorced. That proves a woman's agreement is not needed for a גט. So even if she thinks she is getting a loan document, the גט works, because the husband told the witnesses it was a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not need her consent

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא –
phrases.english: From the testimony of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda we learn:
If he said to witnesses:

phrases.aramaic: רָאוּ גֵּט זֶה שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹתֵן לָהּ,
phrases.english: "See this bill of divorce that I am giving her,"
and then he said to her:
"Take this loan document"
she is divorced.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda say
that we do not need her consent?
Here too we do not need her consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא, building a new ruling on the first testimony
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since a woman's consent is not needed for a גט, a גט given in front of witnesses works even when the husband tells her it is a loan document.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it seems to follow simply from the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: if consent is not needed, of course she is divorced, so why say it? This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling looks like a direct copy of the testimony. The גמרא wants to know what new point he is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's statement in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If consent is not needed, the ruling follows automatically from the testimony and adds nothing new.

steps.title: The new point: calling it a loan document does not cancel the גט
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that calling the גט a loan document cancelled it. רבא teaches that if he meant to cancel it, he would have told the witnesses. He only said it out of embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that since he said 'Take this loan document,' he cancelled the גט. So רבא teaches us: if he really cancelled it, he would have told the witnesses. The reason he said that is because of embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in רבא's ruling: the husband's words to his wife are not a cancellation of the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not about her consent but about his: maybe his words 'loan document' showed he changed his mind. רבא says a real cancellation would have been told to the witnesses, who are the ones the גט depends on. He called it a loan document only because he was embarrassed to tell her directly.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, introducing a mistaken assumption

steps.confusionAlert: The new point here is not about the wife's agreement. It is about whether the husband's own words cancelled the גט.

phrases.english: You might have said,
since he said: "Take this loan document,"
he cancelled the bill of divorce;
so it teaches us:
if it were true that he cancelled it,
he would have told the witnesses.
And the reason he said this to her
is because of embarrassment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר: ״כִּנְסִי שְׁטַר חוֹב זֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden new point (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling the גט a loan document showed the husband cancelled it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cancellation would have been told to the witnesses. His words were only out of embarrassment, so the גט stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A גט does not need the wife's consent, and a husband calling it a 'loan document' out of embarrassment does not cancel it.

steps.title: Inference: a חרשת married to a כהן does not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's mention of only a קטנה בת ישראל, the גמרא learns that a חרשת married to a כהן may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And about a young non-כהן girl': but a deaf-mute woman does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second testimony and notices what it leaves out: a חרשת. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה. Since it did not say the same about a חרשת, the גמרא understands that she does not eat. Both cannot fully agree to a marriage, so the difference needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is a minor
A daughter of a non-כהן family

phrases.english: "And about a minor daughter of a non-priest":
but a deaf-mute woman
does not eat teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל קְטַנָּה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל: וְאִילּוּ חֵרֶשֶׁת – לָא אָכְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the first testimony to the second
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרשת married to a כהן does not eat תרומה.

steps.title: Why may a חרשת not eat תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason a חרשת is treated differently from a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a חרשת married to a כהן cannot eat תרומה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a קטנה and a חרשת lack full understanding, yet only the קטנה eats. The גמרא wants to know what makes the חרשת different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the inference in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a חרשת married to a כהן may not eat תרומה while a קטנה may.

steps.title: A decree so a deaf-mute כהן won't feed his deaf-mute wife
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים made a גזירה that a חרשת does not eat תרומה, so that a חרש כהן will not feed תרומה to a חרשת wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case a deaf-mute man feeds a deaf-mute woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the rule is a rabbinic decree to prevent a different case from going wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חרשת married to a regular כהן could eat, people might let a חרש כהן married to a חרשת feed her too. That marriage is not valid by Torah law, so she would really be eating תרומה forbidden to her. To prevent this, the חכמים said no חרשת eats.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake

phrases.english: It is a decree,
lest a deaf-mute man feed teruma to a deaf-mute woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַאֲכִיל חֵרֵשׁ בְּחֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rabbinic גזירה: if a חרשת could eat, a חרש כהן might feed his חרשת wife, whose marriage is not valid by Torah law.

steps.title: Why worry about a חרשת eating תרומה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the גזירה: a חרשת is like a קטן eating forbidden food, so there should be no reason to stop her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him feed her! She is like a minor who eats forbidden meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given in step 12. Even if a חרש כהן fed תרומה to a חרשת wife, what would be wrong with that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרשת is not legally responsible, just like a קטן. We are not required to stop a קטן who is eating נבלות on his own. So even if she eats תרומה she shouldn't, there seems to be nothing to prevent, and the גזירה looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, who is not legally responsible for מצוות
Meat of animals that died without proper שחיטה, which is forbidden to eat
Then let him feed her (or let her eat)

phrases.english: But let him feed her!
She is like a minor who eats forbidden carcasses!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹיכֵול – קָטָן אוֹכֵל נְבֵלוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 12 for the גזירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה that a חרש כהן might feed תרומה to a חרשת wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חרשת has no legal responsibility, like a קטן eating נבלות, whom we need not stop. So feeding her תרומה is no real problem.

steps.title: The real worry is a חרש feeding a פיקחת wife
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה is really to stop a חרש כהן from feeding תרומה to a normal, competent wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case a deaf-mute man will feed a competent woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the worry. The concern is not the חרשת herself, but a different case that people could mix up with hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a חרש marries a פיקחת, the marriage is only valid מדרבנן, so by Torah law she is not a כהן's wife and may not eat תרומה. Unlike a חרשת, she is fully responsible, so this would be a real sin. If we let a חרשת married to a כהן eat, people might confuse the cases and let the פיקחת eat too.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים
A deaf-mute man, not considered legally competent
A competent woman, who can hear and speak

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: the חכמים sometimes forbid a case that is technically fine so people won't confuse it with a similar case that is really forbidden.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest a deaf-mute man feed a competent woman.
phrases.notes: A חרש's marriage counts only מדרבנן, so his competent wife isn't a כהן's wife by Torah law and truly may not eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַאֲכִיל חֵרֵשׁ בְּפִיקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason for the גזירה to a different, real concern.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה is about the חרשת herself, who isn't responsible anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה protects against a חרש feeding תרומה to a פיקחת wife, who is fully responsible.

steps.title: Let her at least eat rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a חרשת married to a כהן can't at least eat תרומה that is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her eat תרומה that is only rabbinic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the extent of the גזירה. Since her marriage is valid מדרבנן, it should be enough for תרומה that is itself only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of תרומה: from the Torah, and from the חכמים. A marriage that is rabbinic seems strong enough to allow rabbinic תרומה. So why forbid her even that?

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that is required only by the חכמים, not the Torah

phrases.english: But let her eat rabbinic תרומה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹאכֵול בִּתְרוּמָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting the גזירה, asks why it covers even rabbinic תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full ban on a חרשת eating any תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic marriage should be enough to allow rabbinic תרומה.

steps.title: Rabbinic תרומה could lead to Torah תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbade even rabbinic תרומה so that he would not come to feed her Torah תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he comes to feed her Torah-level תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that rabbinic תרומה is also forbidden, as another protective fence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she were allowed rabbinic תרומה, people might not keep the two kinds apart. They could end up feeding her Torah-level תרומה, which her rabbinic marriage does not allow. So the חכמים forbade both.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that is required by the Torah itself

steps.whatToRemember: A חרשת married to a כהן eats no תרומה at all. The חכמים made a fence, and then a second fence, so a חרש would not feed a פיקחת, and rabbinic תרומה would not lead to Torah תרומה.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he come
to feed her Torah-level תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא אָתֵי לְאוֹכוֹלֵי בִּתְרוּמָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes the חרשת discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An extra protective decree (a fence around a fence).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rabbinic marriage should allow rabbinic תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rabbinic תרומה is also forbidden, so people won't come to feed her Torah תרומה.

steps.title: The stolen beam built into a building
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next testimony in the משנה, the stolen beam, and brings a ברייתא where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the stolen beam that he built into a building: The Rabbis taught: If someone stole a beam and built it into a building, בית שמאי say he must tear down the whole building and give the beam back to its owner. בית הלל say the owner gets only the value of the beam, because of a rule made to help people who want to do תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and brings a ברייתא to explain it. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say a stolen item must be returned exactly as it is, even if a whole building must come down. בית הלל say paying the value is enough, so that a thief who wants to do תשובה won't be scared off by the huge cost. The משנה's ruling, that the owner gets only the money, follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made to help those who want to do תשובה

steps.whyThisMatters: תקנת השבים is a key idea in the laws of stealing: the חכמים eased the rules so that people would not be discouraged from repenting.

phrases.english: And about the stolen beam that he built in:
The Rabbis taught:
If one stole a beam and built it into a building,
בית שמאי say:
He must tear down the entire building
and return the beam to its owner;
and בית הלל say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא דְּמֵי מָרִישׁ בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: He (the owner) gets only the value of the beam,
because of the rule made for those who repent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַמָּרִישׁ הַגָּזוּל שֶׁבְּנָאוֹ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חרשת discussion to the next testimony in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: tear down the building and return the beam. בית הלל: pay only the beam's value, because of תקנת השבים.

steps.title: עולא: By Torah law a stolen sin-offering never atones
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that by תורה law a stolen חטאת does not bring כפרה, whether or not people know it was stolen, because יאוש alone does not let the robber acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the stolen חטאת mentioned in the משנה: עולא said that by תורה law, whether people know it was stolen or not, it does not bring כפרה. Why? Because the owner giving up hope (יאוש) is not enough on its own to make the animal belong to the robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, a stolen חטאת, and brings עולא's view of what the תורה law really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a stolen חטאת atones if it is not publicly known. עולא says that by the תורה it never atones, because the animal still belongs to the original owner. The owner's יאוש does not move ownership to the robber, so the robber is offering an animal that isn't his.

keyTerms.meaning: By תורה law (as opposed to a rabbinic rule)
It became known (that the animal was stolen)
The owner giving up hope of getting his item back
Despair alone does not give the robber ownership

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not arguing with the משנה's ruling. He agrees that when it isn't known the חטאת atones, but he says that is only a rabbinic rule. By the תורה itself, it never atones.

phrases.english: And about a stolen sin-offering, etc.
Ulla said:
By Torah law,
whether it is known or it is not known,
it does not atone.
What is the reason?
Despair by itself does not acquire.
phrases.notes: כדי here means 'just like that': the owner's despair alone, with no change to the animal, doesn't make it the robber's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, בֵּין נוֹדְעָה וּבֵין לֹא נוֹדְעָה – אֵינָהּ מְכַפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the stolen beam to the next testimony in the משנה, the stolen חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law a stolen חטאת never atones, because יאוש alone does not transfer ownership to the robber.

steps.title: Why the חכמים let an unknown stolen offering atone
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the חכמים ruled that an unknown stolen חטאת atones so that the כהנים would not be upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why did the חכמים say that if it isn't known, it atones? So that the כהנים would not be upset.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains where the משנה's rule comes from, since by his view the תורה itself says it doesn't atone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה says it doesn't atone, the משנה's rule must be a rabbinic enactment. עולא gives the reason: the כהנים would be upset to learn they had offered an animal that was not fit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: And why did they (the חכמים) say

phrases.english: And what is the reason they said:
if it is not known, it atones?
So that the priests will not be upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה טַעַם אָמְרוּ: לֹא נוֹדְעָה מְכַפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues עולא's statement by explaining the rabbinic basis for the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that an unknown stolen חטאת atones is rabbinic, made so that the כהנים would not be upset.

steps.title: רבנן: the משנה says it is for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge עולא: the משנה gives the reason as 'for the sake of the מזבח', not for the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to עולא: But we learned in the משנה that the reason is 'for the sake of the מזבח'!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack עולא's reason by pointing to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the rule was made for the כהנים' feelings. But the משנה says it was made 'for the sake of the מזבח'. That sounds like a different reason, so עולא's explanation seems to clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of (the proper running of) the altar

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Ulla:
But didn't we learn: "for the sake of the altar"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְעוּלָּא: וְהָאֲנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason עולא gave in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason that the rule is so the כהנים won't be upset.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names the מזבח as the reason, not the כהנים, so עולא's reason seems to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: עולא: Upset priests leave the altar idle
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that both reasons are really the same: if the כהנים are upset, the מזבח ends up unused.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to them: Since the כהנים would be upset, the מזבח would end up idle.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends his reason by showing it fits the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Upset כהנים would hold back from bringing offerings, so the מזבח would stand idle. Caring for the כהנים' feelings is really caring for the מזבח. The two reasons are one.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out, the result is

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, a stolen חטאת atones only by rabbinic rule, and only when it isn't known. The rule protects the כהנים, and through them the מזבח.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Since the priests are upset,
the altar is found to be idle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כֵּיוָן דְּכֹהֲנִים עֲצֵבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the two reasons are one: concern for the כהנים is concern for the מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן thought 'for the sake of the מזבח' was a separate reason from the כהנים' feelings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Upset כהנים would leave the מזבח idle, so the משנה's wording fits עולא's reason.

steps.title: רב יהודה: By Torah law a stolen sin-offering always atones
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה disagrees with עולא: by תורה law a stolen חטאת atones whether or not it is known, because יאוש alone does give the robber ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: By תורה law, whether it is known or not, it atones. Why? Because the owner's יאוש by itself makes the animal belong to the robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite view of the תורה law from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא and רב יהודה disagree about one point: does יאוש alone transfer ownership? רב יהודה says yes. Once the owner gives up hope, the animal is the robber's and he can offer it properly, so it atones even by תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: Despair alone does give the robber ownership

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on יאוש: עולא says יאוש alone doesn't acquire, so the offering doesn't atone by תורה law. רב יהודה says יאוש alone does acquire, so it atones.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
By Torah law,
whether it is known or not known,
it atones.
What is the reason?
Despair by itself acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, בֵּין נוֹדְעָה בֵּין לֹא נוֹדְעָה – מְכַפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to עולא's statement in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law a stolen חטאת atones in all cases, because יאוש alone transfers ownership to the robber.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question in the laws of stealing: whether the owner's יאוש alone, without any change to the item, makes the stolen item the robber's.
